iteration_0_negative_result.description: Twelve proposition-near queries over the 17-claim ledger were too easy to discriminate retrieval mechanisms.

iteration_1_semantic_stress.description: Eleven query families are derived from existing topic_packet identifiers rather than claim proposition wording. Expected sets are exactly the current claims sharing the packet. Real bootstrap chunks compete as lexical distractors. All strategies use max budget k=5.

supported: For topic-packet semantic-anchor queries on this current Clay content snapshot, a precompiled exact family plus sufficiency-stop dominates the tested FTS5/BM25 claim-filter baseline on precision, MRR, nDCG and median retrieval latency while matching recall.
Padding a semantically complete field back to top-k measurably destroys precision and adds latency; no-padding is therefore a causal mechanism candidate rather than a presentation preference.
not_supported: Universal superiority over every database, vector database, graph database or retrieval system.
Generalization to arbitrary natural-language queries without semantic-anchor resolution.
Live FRANK downstream answer or action-quality improvement.

architecture_delta.rule: When an epoch-coherent VERIFIED/CURRENT compiled semantic generation has a non-empty field for the resolved seed, return that field without lexical top-k padding. Otherwise fall back to measured conventional retrieval.
architecture_delta.rollback: Disable V11 semantic generation head or remove sufficient-field branch; canonical UnifiedDB truth is unchanged.

next_falsifiers: Held-out real Clay natural-language queries whose semantic anchors are independently adjudicated rather than derived from topic_packet strings.
Stale, missing, contradictory and untrusted graph-edge injections.
Dense/late-interaction and PostgreSQL FTS+pgvector matched-budget baselines.
Hostinger Ubuntu and Andreas target execution.
